extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in personality psychology and humor research, especially those studying adolescents
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical research examining the temperamental basis of humor (cheerfulness, seriousness, bad mood) versus broad Big Five personality traits as predictors of everyday humor behaviors and subjective well-being in adolescents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperamental basis of humor: cheerfulness, seriousness, bad mood
rubrics_metrics.description: The three traits known as the temperamental basis of humor (cheerfulness, seriousness, and bad mood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via the STCI‑youth; these narrower temperament traits are hypothesized to predict everyday humor behaviors and well‑being and to be useful constructs for investigating individual differences in humor among adolescents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑factor model (Big Five) personality traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad personality traits as defined by the five‑factor model, measured here with the IPIP‑junior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a set of broader, competing predictors to compare against the narrower temperamental traits; included as control/predictor variables in analyses to test incremental validity of temperament measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction of unique variance (incremental validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traits assessed by the STCI‑youth "predicted unique variance in both the frequency of humor behaviors and well‑being – beyond demographic variables, the personality traits of the five‑factor model, and each other."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic standard: show that a targeted trait explains variance in outcome measures over and above demographics and broad personality traits; report unique predictive effects rather than only zero‑order correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dominance analysis for relative importance of predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of dominance analysis (Azen & Budescu, 2003; Budescu, 1993) to compare predictors in multiple regression and determine which variables 'outperform' others in accounting for variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply dominance analysis to establish the relative importance of predictors (e.g., cheerfulness and seriousness for humor behaviors; cheerfulness and bad mood for well‑being), rather than relying solely on standardized betas or p‑values.

rubrics_metrics.name: STCI‑youth (state‑ and trait‑cheerfulness inventory — youth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionnaire assessing the traits of cheerfulness, seriousness, and bad mood in youth (state‑ and trait versions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the STCI‑youth to operationalize the temperamental basis of humor; ensure use of validated translations/forms and report psychometric properties (construction and validation referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPIP‑junior (Big Five measure for youth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrument used to measure the five‑factor model personality traits in children/adolescents (IPIP‑junior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as the operationalization of broad personality traits for comparison; report reliability and how scores were used in regression/dominance analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUMOR: frequency of everyday humor behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of the frequency with which participants typically displayed 13 different humor behaviors (labelled HUMOR in the study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this or comparable behavioral frequency measures to capture everyday humorous conduct; specify items, scoring, and psychometrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWI‑SC (Personal Wellbeing Index — School Children) for well‑being
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrument used to assess subjective well‑being in school‑aged children/adolescents (PWI‑SC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated well‑being scales appropriate for the age group and report psychometric indices and scoring procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample description and demographic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sample size and demographics (here: N = 379 adolescents aged 10 to 17 years, mean age = 15.52, 28.5% male).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide age range, mean age, sex distribution, and other relevant demographics; include how participants were recruited and any inclusion/exclusion criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and disclosure (informed consent and conflicts of interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical statement that informed consent was obtained from each participant and conflict of interest disclosure (authors declare no conflict of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report institutional ethics approval, informed consent procedures appropriate for minors, and any conflicts of interest or funding disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant/construct validity: overlap with but distinct from Big Five
rubrics_metrics.description: The temperamental traits 'overlap with broad personality traits, while being unique predictors of everyday humor behaviors and well‑being.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate both convergence (overlap) and discriminant validity (unique predictive power) of temperament measures relative to broad personality constructs; include multivariate analyses that partition shared and unique variance.
